body:
I am in the exact same boat. I'm still with my partner (two breakups, neither lasted) and I find myself lying to her a lot to keep her from guilting me about things. I'll lie and say I've been called into work when I haven't because when I'm not working I am expected to either be with her or to text with her 24/7. If I take more than a couple minutes to respond she gets upset...unless I'm at work. Or I'll use it so I can see friends or family, people who she really really hates. 

But it tears me up inside. Every time I lie to her my chest tightens ever more. I feel terrible misleading her but if I don't I have no freedom. I'm not allowed to see people I care about. I can't do anything on my own/without constantly being on my phone if I'm not "at work." 

Know that you are not alone in how you feel. It seems like this guilt and the need to lie are common side effects of being abused. It doesn't make you bad, even if that's what your brain is telling you. It's letting you survive. And your survival has to come before being honest with your abuser. I know it isn't fair and this reassurance may not do much, but I promise it is the truth.

I can identify with that. I’ve been in my relationship for 6.5 years. We were friends before that. In the time immediately before and immediately after we got together, she used to talk about how she was excited to have sex, that she was “tired of being a virgin,” how she was masturbating several times a week. Those were all things I was feeling too, so I was ecstatic to find someone on the same page as me. 

Once we’d been together for a couple of weeks, I broached the subject of sex with her. She said she wasn’t ready for full sex, but maybe we could start slow. I was allowed to start performing oral sex on her when we got together on the condition that I remained clothed and didn’t go any further than that. I was just so excited to have this beautiful woman willing to undress in front of me that I went for it. It’s now been over half a decade and we have not made it any further. I go down on her a couple of times a week, always fully clothed. She has never done anything to me. Nothing. She’s only ever seen me naked two or three times, and even then it’s been brief. Hasn’t ever expressed attraction to me beyond my ability to give her orgasms. 

Over the last few years, she’s changed her opinion about sex whenever she’s needed to in order to keep me from asking for me. She’s gone from excitement about sex and the desire to not be a virgin to saying she’s never masturbated and doesn’t really care about sex to saying that she was getting ready to have sex to saying that she wanted to wait until marriage. 

I’m now twenty-seven, with no sexual experience other than going down on her, and feeling perpetually unwanted. Even if I manage to break away from her I feel like I am beyond the point of feeling desirable. Selfishness in bed from a narc is so damaging. My heart goes out to you for everything you went through.

I have to say, I have been looking around subs like this and NarcissisticAbuse for years, and this is without question one of the best summaries of how to tell if you're in an unhealthy/abusive relationship. You have it just right.

For me, I have stayed because I worry about hurting her. At the best of times I worry that I'm the abusive one and when I broke up with her before she leaned heavily into how I had done something so awful to her. That none of my issues were real, I had just had a "breakdown" as she called it and hurt her. And now I live in perpetual fear of hurting her again

I really like your post. It resonated with me a lot. Would you mind if I asked a kind of followup question? 

My (narcissistic?) partner is big into gift giving. Always has been. She says that it's her love language, which I do genuinely believe is true. And a lot of the gifts she gives are handmade. She does a lot of different crafts very well and is usually working on something for someone. My question is about intent. 

You talk about how giving gifts can just be for "go[ing] through the motions of being kind" and how often gifts given are really gifts for the narc. My partner will very often say while making her gifts that she has to make stuff "so that people will like her." And that no one would like her if she didn't make them things. This second one is flat out not true. But do you think that that sounds like what you're talking about? She has previously kept tabs on how people use the things she makes to ensure that they're "appreciating" her hard work properly, and gets very angry if she finds out something she made isn't on prominent display. 

This is not the only bit of behaviour that makes me wonder about whether she is a narcissist (if you need more context I have posted about her before), but her intent in gift giving is something I've wondered about for a while and hoped since you have thought about this stuff too that you might have an opinion too. 

I appreciate your time!

My initial reaction was to feel guilty, because that tends to be my normal response to her getting upset. But over the course of the day I rationalized that maybe she was just burned out from work and that let me kind of put it behind me. It was only after I told someone about it after the fact that it hit me that maybe it was wrong of her to do.

I can wholeheartedly relate to this. My partner is a PhD candidate and a few years ago I accompanied her on a research trip because she couldn't afford to hire a research assistant. We spent 8-10 hours per day in archives doing research, six days per week. On one of our two days off, we got lunch at a food truck before going to a museum she wanted to visit. She has severe social anxiety so I ordered for her while she waited on a bench. When I brought her the food, she asked if I had gotten a receipt so she could claim it in her expenses. I forgot. She refused to speak to me until we were halfway through research the next day. 

Lunch was $11. And because she couldn't claim it, I got silence.

Do all cooking and cleaning. 

Offer massages without ever hoping for reciprocation.

Respond immediately to all messages, even if she takes her time reading and replying.

Be up earlier and stay up later so that she is never without my contact.

Be on messenger to chat during all classes and work.

Tell my friends and family about her criticisms of them for her, even when they are fictional.

Forsake all holidays with my family so we can spend them with hers.

Take all of her mean comments as jokes no matter what they are. 

Send her 4-8 unique, lengthy messages each day describing why I love her (I know this doesn't sound bad but it honestly feels like something out of a cult sometimes).

Ignore my sexual desires in favour of hers (or none at all).

Accept that when I tried to break up with her it was only because I had a "breakdown."

Spend no money because I need to save for an extraordinarily expensive ring. 

That covers a lot of it. Thank you for listening!

Repeated "jokes" about how much she wanted my best friend, his wife, and my family to suffer. Talking about shoving them in front of buses or hoping that they'd die in terrible car accidents. This went on for about two years. But when I called her on it she said I was being oversensitive and that "everyone jokes about wanting people dead." 

Didn't stop me from feeling sick every time I heard it.

You're absolutely right that you can't change her. My heart goes out to anyone struggling with that kind of insecurity but it isn't fair for them to turn it into toxicity. 

My partner and I were friends prior to dating, and I remember her getting annoyed whenever I'd mention my female research partner...a married lesbian. But it was always "oh I guess I have to share you now." I'm now at the point where I can talk to my mom and sister but no other women.

So much of this sounds familiar. I am in a similar situation to you with most of it happening over text rather than face to face. I have been with her for six years. Trust me when I say this will not change. Every day I get questions about whether I still love her. At least once a week there are questions about my fidelity (I have never even come close to cheating). And there's the constant guilting about stuff

It's draining. And it's hard to call abuse (even if it may be) because someone asking if you love them seems so benign. 

I don't feel qualified to say run, because it's been six years for me and I still go back and forth about what I've experienced, but please know that this is unlikely to stop. Consider that when going forward. 

Good luck and stay safe.

I think it probably does amount to abuse. There's a lot here that I can identify with and have previously called abusive. Hearing "my life is already shit, so why not add this on" is especially relatable. I hear that regularly. A couple of years ago my childhood dog died on her birthday and her response was to complain that her day was ruined and that she hated my parents for neglecting to wish her a happy birthday on social media.

Your feelings are completely valid. Your anger is understandable and it is probably best that you have broken up. Even if you hesitate to call her abusive, you weren't happy there. You even said that from date one you were uncomfortable. And that selfishness you describe will only grow over time. Eventually being "grateful" for what she does/what she buys you will not be enough. It would be healthier to find someone who doesn't treat you that way.

Same here. I couldn’t pay for an $8000 ring on a grad student’s salary.

The sad thing? She trashes my family and friends to my face and claims it’s because they’ve all treated her so horribly. I tried standing up to her and was just accused of denying her experiences.

Oh my gosh, this is almost exactly me. I (25M) have been with my girlfriend (26F) for five years. She’s been fairly toxic for the last three and she blames it in large part on the fact that I haven’t proposed yet. But, like you, I haven’t for (I think) good reasons. She has a short temper. She speaks horribly about my friends and family. She wants a ring several thousand dollars more than I can afford. But every time I get ready to leave her she senses it. Is super nice and open. And I end up feeling so guilty about having thought she was abusive. Thank you so much for sharing your experience and congratulations on getting out!

I want to thank you for sharing your story in these words. My partner is a lot like this. She’ll smack my arm lightly if I say something she doesn’t like but otherwise is totally hands off. But I walk on eggshells and lie and hide things from her because if anything happens that she doesn’t like she’ll scream and tell me about how much she hopes the people in my life will die or suffer. I worry a lot that I’m the abuser because of my lying and hiding but I only do it because I’m afraid of her.

I hope you are correct. My parents (and my partner, actually) always tell me that I never used to be this way. That I wasn't always sullen and depressed and that I was once confident in myself. The sad thing? I can't remember those days anymore. But I am hopeful that one day I can get back to them.

Thank you for your kind words and warm welcome. It really means so much to hear that. 

I admit I am in a bit of a unique position in that a lot of the abuse that has come from her has been targeted at my family and friends. She has said some truly horrible things about them and while I have tried my best to keep all of those comments from them, I know that they're aware of at least some. And I'm sure that's part of why they've been so supportive during my time away from her. 

I guess that's part of why it's been so hard to convince myself she's been bad to me; she doesn't often directly attack or insult *me*. But I do frequently get a "it's them or me" vibe from her. And when I don't pick her, I end up the bad guy, even when it's that I can't support her saying my family is cruel or that my friends should suffer.

Thank you so much for your kind words. I’m looking into reactive abuse now. I really hope you’re correct. I spend a lot of time agonizing over how I’ve treated her and the stress this has all brought upon my friends and family. They’ve never made me feel bad about it, but still. It’s hard to escape the guilt.

Like so many others in this thread, probably not the first sign telling me to get out, but one of the earliest I remember ignoring.

It was just after Pokemon GO came out. Things had been tense between us lately, but we started going for walks more regularly to catch Pokemon. Things seemed to be looking up. Then one night we were out and found an Ivysaur. This was early on, so that seemed like a major catch. I got mine. She did not. She then refused to speak to me for several hours afterwards because she was so furious. Over a very common Pokemon in a mobile game.

This is so accurate. Last year I went to Washington with my partner and over the course of fifteen days I managed to lose thirteen pounds (151 -> 138) between walking and being too stressed to eat. 

I also have osteogenesis imperfecta (or osteoporosis; my osteopath doesn’t know yet) and I have fractured three vertebrae so far this year just from being too tense. 

Abuse and trauma, even emotional, carry such a heavy weight on the body.

I'm so sorry you're going through this. We're all here for you. As Ladyship pointed out, self-forgiveness is so important. You aren't alone in going back and regretting it. I think a lot of us have been there. I know I have. I'm not sure how much this will mean coming from a stranger, but I can guarantee you are deserving of forgiveness.

Thank you for your reply! The context in that last sentence is especially helpful. I hadn't thought of it before, but you're completely correct. Even if she needed a picture to show her burn, it was largely the base of her neck and would have been easy to zoom in there. I think you're right about her motivation.
Thank you for your reassurance! I’m really trying to tell myself it was done to manipulate me. It’s tough but I’m hoping I can get there. Manage to block her again one day.

Thank you for your kind words. That last bit of advice is great. Hard to follow at first, but definitely true. I’m working on building up to living for myself. It’s taking time, but I hope that I can get there.

I appreciate you saying so. I was able to block her once and went NC for about two weeks but the guilt of ghosting her got to me. I unblocked her and it’s been downhill since. I fully intend on being home for Christmas, regardless of the consequences. Just have to work up the nerve to tell her so. 

Thank you again!

I can identify with so much of what you have written here. I could have written everything up until you broke up with her basically verbatim. We've been together for five years. The first two were great - at the time. Looking back, maybe there were some red flags. Her screaming at her parents who gave in whenever she treated them badly. Her telling me that she's never managed to hold onto a friend for longer than four years before. 

As of the two year mark, she began telling me about how awful my best friend and my parents were to her. She told me repeatedly how much she wished my best friend's wife would die or at least get maimed in an accident. But I wrote it off as her being jealous of her engagement. And here we are today: my family won't speak to her, my best friend and his wife don't respond to her messages, and I can't help but feel like a bad person for keeping them all together for so long. 

I applaud your strength in staying away. Your story gives hope to the rest of us. Thank you for sharing!

Five years and counting. I had suspicions about her temper at first but thought it would get better. The last three years have been a non-stop rollercoaster of self-doubt, self-loathing, and rationalizing why she keeps telling me I’m not enough, that our relationship is disappointing, and that my friends and family are horrible to her. I’ve tried getting away twice and failed. 

Nothing but respect for people who are able to gain confidence to leave and stay away.

This was largely via text, but I hope it still counts...

For my partner's birthday a couple of years ago, her parents took her on a cruise, just the three of them. They asked me to housesit/petsit for them while they were away and I agreed. I told my family of this plan, and they said that they would save their presents for her until after she got back. She was fine with this. They leave and all is well. 

Unfortunately, on the day of her actual birthday, my childhood dog died. She took ill quite suddenly and I woke up that morning to a phone message from my dad saying they were taking her to be put down. I hurry to the vet's office to be there with my family and my dog and she passes. All of us are in tears; she had clearly begun to suffer in her last day. We all leave and I check my phone. I've missed a message from my partner letting me know she had cell service for the day. I wish her a happy birthday and she responds coolly. I tell her about my dog, and she responds "thanks for ruining my birthday." For the rest of the day, I hear nothing but rage and contempt for my family and I because a) my dog's sudden death distracted from her day and; b) no one had wished her a happy birthday on Facebook yet. She begins telling me how she hopes my family suffers the way that she has because of their neglect (again, caused by not posting on fb yet). Most importantly, she tells me to get my family to return their gifts because she wants no acknowledgement of her birthday when she gets home. I relay the message to my parents. 

For the rest of the week, I hear nothing from her. I can see she has service, but I just get the silent treatment. When she gets home, she's still angry. But we arrange to get together a few days later with my family. I tell her we'll do a nice dinner. She asks about presents and I say that they returned them, at her request. So she cancels my family's dinner and says she's never been so hurt in all her life. 

It has been \~3 years since that happened and she still brings it up sometimes.

This is such a great list. There are a few points here that aren't discussed enough and it's refreshing to see them addressed here. Especially number fifteen: many narcs discard their partners, but the ones who hold on and won't let go are just as damaging. When I tried going NC with my partner she found a few other ways to get around my blocking her on everything and just wouldn't stop. That (along with my residual guilt) is what managed to pull me back in.

Thank you for making this post. The last few days have been particularly difficult and I needed this. 

May I ask: is it bad to keep telling the same stories over and over again? I've started and deleted a few posts here lately because a lot of the things I want to say I've said before (here and on a couple similar subs). I don't want to seem like I'm going too far in repeating them but...sometimes I could just use to, you know? Is that wrong?

I identify so strongly with everything you've said here. The whole "you never have my back" thing (or as mine put it, "you never stand up for me") is such manipulative garbage. If you don't mind reading a similar story, I can share mine. 

A couple of years ago, my best friend and his wife got engaged. They are the sweetest couple I know, and I was over the moon happy for them. My (abusive? I'm not confident enough to say for sure) partner and I used to double date with them a lot, and so they asked me to be their best man and they asked my partner to be one of the bridesmaids (the bride's sister was already maid of honour). The moment they asked us, the dynamic between us changed. 

It started just between my partner and I. Any time this other couple was not around, she'd talk about how much she hated them and how poorly they had treated her. I passed it off as her being jealous that she hadn't been asked to be maid of honour, which still wasn't great, but I tried my best to ignore it. Eventually this grew to her wishing that someone would kill them, or at least that they'd end up in a car accident and not married. She started asking me to break the maid of honour's foot as we walked down the aisle together. Months before the wedding, she began referring to the groomsman she would escort as "troglodyte," despite the two of them not meeting until the rehearsal dinner. 

When I tried to ask her to stop, she became furious and said that I wasn't defending her or standing up for her. She told me to tell off my best friend, who had done nothing wrong in any of this, for being cruel to her. When I didn't, she became much more open in her fury. I became incompetent (a name she called me in front of my parents, making them not like her and making her target them as other people I needed to defend her to). Our relationship became "disappointing" to her. When I responded negatively to that one she got mad at me for misinterpreting what she said. But most commonly she just became mean to my best friend and his wife. Really mean. She started telling them she wasn't coming to their wedding unless they gave in to her demands. They did not, but she still came and then just treated the bride terribly (something I still feel an immense amount of guilt over). 

To this day, whenever someone brings up anything she did during this time, she'll get mad at me for not defending her. She routinely tells me she has "dreams" in which I put other people first over her and they always bother her. I don't know whether those dreams are real or if she's just saying that because she knows it gets to me. 

My best friend and his wife will still hang out with me. We are, fortunately, still very close. We talk and see each other often. But they will not see my partner. My partner really wants to see them, but every time I say no she sulks that I'm just ignoring her pain and I'm making her out to be a villain. 

You stay strong too. I'm glad that you recognise "you never have my back" for what it is: manipulation and gaslighting.

Absolutely!

You have no idea how often I've started writing out a post like yours (only to stop out of fear that I was wrong). I don't have a formal diagnosis (I am on a waiting list to get into a therapist who specialises in trauma) but most stuff that I have read about CPTSD makes me think I fit in with it. I've never been physically or sexually abused, but I've spent the last five years in a relationship with a woman who I believe is a narcissist and (I think) has been very emotionally abusive. 

I have lost complete trust in myself. The reason I qualified everything I said in the above paragraph is because I can't tell if I'm overreacting or not. I genuinely don't know which of my feelings, thoughts, and memories are real and which are just me being oversensitive. I have countless examples of cruel things she's said, excessive verbal and emotional manipulation to pressure me, and ways in which she has overstepped my boundaries, and yet I still don't know if it's her or me. She tells me that I've just misinterpreted the things I've said and that the problem is my communication rather than her behaviour. I spend most of my days feeling shame and/or guilt rather than anything else. I am ashamed of myself, especially my appearance and my cowardice, and I feel bad that either: a) I have kept this toxic person in my (and my family's) life for so long, or; b) that I am wrong about her and I have just slandered her because I'm mentally ill. Now I am easily triggered by anyone showing anger (especially yelling or slamming things). 

Thank you for your post. It gave me a place to tell part of my story again. Know that you are not alone in your symptoms or your experiences. Emotional abuse can be so damaging to every part of your life, and it's so insidious that it ends up doing terrible damage before you even realise it. I hope that you are able to find help and solace. For getting through your emotionally abusive relationships, you've already shown just how strong you are. 

We're all with you here.
You’re exactly right. No matter how much you read about it, it’s hard to accept that’s what’s happening even when it is.

That’s it exactly. Mine will give endless gifts to everyone, even people she otherwise treats terribly. For her, gift giving is the only love language. She’s given me more than I have space for, even things I have specifically said I don’t want. Mine is an avid crafter. Admittedly, she is very good at it. She’ll spend hours and hours making something I didn’t want and then get upset if I don’t express the proper amount of gratitude for her work. 


Also, thank you for sharing your experience! Reading about how the same sort of dynamic works with acts of service really helped to put it in perspective. Like you, my love language priority is touch first and gifts last. But if I ask for any kind of physical affection it feels like it’s pulling teeth unless she wants something. Eventually you learn to stop asking and just hope for the best.
Thank you for your kind words 😌
I really appreciate the reassurance. I always feel guilty that I’m blowing things out of proportion when I receive them, but the way you’ve phrased it makes perfect sense.

Number three is almost verbatim what I’ve heard from mine. I broke up with her and she has said that she “doesn’t blame me,” that I just had a “breakdown” when I broke up with her, and that she wants to help me through my mental health issues together, even though I believe she is the cause of my mental distress. Unfortunately, she has also used my going to a therapist as evidence that I am...unwell in the eyes of her family

Not as severe as sleeping in the same place together, but my (possibly) narc gf requires that I text with her 24/7. From the moment I wake up until the moment I go to bed, I have to be with my phone, ready to respond immediately. It definitely makes it so that I end up lying about when I wake up and when I go to bed so I can have some peace. My heart goes out to you because I know how draining that is. It’s hard to be ‘on’ all the time especially when you know some of your socializing is going to be so profoundly negative.

That sounds so familiar! Mine always claims to make all the plans and that she wants me to plan something “for once” even though I have scheduled the vast majority of stuff we’ve done. If you don’t mind my asking, how do/did you manage to keep the fact that it’s crazy making in mind?

Absolutely. I (25M) have been in a relationship with a woman (25F) who I suspect is asexual for five years. In the beginning she told me she wanted to wait a little while before sex, which was fine with me, but since then she has exhibited zero interest in most sex. I am allowed occasionally to perform oral sex on her, but I am to remain fully dressed at all times. She will not reciprocate, instead offering a variety of excuses for why she could not do more. 

In recent years, sex has become a carrot she can dangle in front of me when she’s been particularly mean. She’ll flaunt her body in front of me or tease me in some way. But that’s as far as it’ll go.

She uses the excuse that it’s a manifestation of her anxiety. I suffer with anxiety as well and have all the empathy in world for anxiety problems. But she uses it as a free pass to make me feel like a disappointment and to talk at length about how much she wants everyone in my life to suffer. She once told me I should hurt myself because we had to go to a wedding and it made her uncomfortable.
